# Demo video pipeline (VHS + recorded voiceover)

Turn a demo script into a narrated MP4 (the user's voiceover synced to a terminal
recording) plus silent GIF/WebM assets for docs. The pipeline lives in
[`tools/demo/videos/`](../../../tools/demo/videos) and is driven by a single manifest.

## Core idea — the beat is the unit of sync

VHS has no audio, and human narration timing varies per take. So each demo is split into
**beats**: a chunk of on-screen action + one line of narration. Each beat is rendered to
its own silent clip and recorded to its own audio clip; at build time the video's last
frame is **frozen** to match the audio length (plus a short tail). This guarantees the
video never outpaces the voice and lets any single beat be re-recorded independently.

```
manifest ─▶ render.mjs ─▶ silent beat clips + full GIF/WebM
manifest ─▶ record.mjs ─▶ one .wav per beat (teleprompter + mic)
            build.mjs  ─▶ pad video→audio, mux, concat ─▶ <slug>.narrated.mp4 + .srt/.vtt
```

## Prerequisites

* `vhs` (`brew install vhs`) and `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` (`brew install ffmpeg`) on PATH.
* For CLI/TUI demos the binary must build; the manifest's `prebuild` handles this
  (mirrors `tools/demo/verify-demo.sh`).

## 1. Author or edit a manifest

Manifests are zero-dependency ES modules: `tools/demo/videos/<slug>.demo.mjs`. Start from
[`cli-quickstart.demo.mjs`](../../../tools/demo/videos/cli-quickstart.demo.mjs). The full
schema is documented in [`lib/tape.mjs`](../../../tools/demo/videos/lib/tape.mjs):

```js
export default {
  title: "design-data CLI — quickstart",
  slug: "cli-quickstart",            // filename-safe basename for all outputs
  width: 1280, height: 720, fontSize: 22,
  theme: "Catppuccin Mocha", typingSpeed: "60ms",
  prebuild: ["cargo build --release --manifest-path sdk/Cargo.toml --bin design-data"],
  setup: ['export PATH="$PWD/sdk/target/release:$PATH"', "clear"], // hidden per beat
  beats: [
    {
      id: "component",                // stable slug → <slug>-component.mp4/.wav
      narration: "One sentence spoken over this beat.",
      tape: `Type "design-data component button --components-dir packages/design-data/components"
Enter
Wait
Sleep 3s`,
    },
  ],
};
```

Authoring guidance:

* **Source the script.** For the CLI use [`tools/demo/scenarios.md`](../../../tools/demo/scenarios.md)
  (commands + "Say:" lines). For the TUI use [`sdk/tui/DEMO.md`](../../../sdk/tui/DEMO.md)
  (keystroke tables → VHS `Type`/`Enter`/`Tab`/arrow commands; `:` opens the palette).
* **One idea per beat.** Keep narration to \~1–2 sentences; the build pads the clip to fit.
* **Keep the punchline on screen.** If a command floods the terminal (e.g. `validate`
  prints the whole corpus), filter it so the key line stays visible:
  `... 2>&1 | grep -A1 SPEC-001`.
* **Pacing (VHS 3-2-1 rule).** End each beat's actions with `Wait` then `Sleep` (≈3s after
  a key result, 2s between actions). `Type@30ms "..."` overrides typing speed inline.
* **Setup stays hidden.** Put build/PATH/`clear` in `prebuild` (run once, outside VHS) and
  `setup` (run in a hidden block at the start of every beat).

## 2. Render the silent assets

```bash
node tools/demo/videos/render.mjs [tools/demo/videos/<slug>.demo.mjs]
#  --beat <id>     render only one beat (repeatable)   --no-prebuild   skip cargo build
#  --no-full       skip the GIF/WebM doc render
```

Produces `out/<slug>-<beat>.mp4` (per beat) and `out/<slug>.gif` + `out/<slug>.webm`.
Verify a frame before recording: `ffmpeg -sseof -1 -i out/<slug>-<beat>.mp4 -frames:v 1 /tmp/f.png`.

## 3. Record the voiceover (the user, not TTS)

This step is interactive and belongs to the user. Tell them to run:

```bash
node tools/demo/videos/record.mjs [<manifest>]   # teleprompter; Enter to start/stop a beat
#  --list-devices   list mic inputs        --device <idx>   choose input
#  --beat <id> --force   re-record one beat
```

For pipeline testing only (do NOT ship as the user's voice), you may synthesize placeholder
audio: `node tools/demo/videos/record.mjs --say`. The user can also hand-drop their own
`out/<slug>-<beat>.wav` files instead of using the recorder.

## 4. Build the narrated video

```bash
node tools/demo/videos/build.mjs [<manifest>]
#  --tail <seconds>   silence held after each beat (default 0.5)
#  --burn             also emit <slug>.captioned.mp4 with burned-in subtitles
```

Outputs `out/<slug>.narrated.mp4` plus `out/<slug>.srt` and `out/<slug>.vtt`. To re-record
one beat: rerun `record.mjs --beat <id> --force`, then `build.mjs` again.

## Moon tasks

`moon run demo:videos-render`, `demo:videos-record`, `demo:videos-build` wrap the scripts
(see [`tools/demo/moon.yml`](../../../tools/demo/moon.yml)). Pass a manifest with `-- <path>`.

## Conventions

* New `.mjs` files need the Adobe Apache-2.0 header with the **current year** (see existing
  files in `tools/demo/videos/`).
* Outputs in `tools/demo/videos/out/` are gitignored (re-buildable). Commit only curated,
  published assets, and only if explicitly asked.
* This is the video workflow; the asciinema notes in `sdk/tui/DEMO.md` predate it. VHS is
  preferred here because it outputs MP4 directly for muxing.

## Gotchas

* VHS can fail with `could not open ttyd … ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` on a cold start right
  after a long build — `render.mjs` already retries; just re-run if it slips through.
* Keep audio as PCM until mux; `padAudioTo` writes `pcm_s16le` wav, and `mux` encodes AAC.
* Output paths in VHS `Output` are relative to the working directory (repo root here).

***

# Live presentation deck (asciinema casts + Slidev)

When the goal is a **live demo while screen-sharing** (not a pre-narrated MP4), use the
Slidev deck under [`tools/demo/presentation/`](../../../tools/demo/presentation) instead
of the VHS pipeline. The presenter narrates each beat in person; the embedded terminal
**pauses at every beat marker** and resumes on click.

## Core idea — markers drive the pauses

asciinema records the full TUI (alternate screen) losslessly into a tiny text `.cast`.
Drop a **marker** at each beat boundary while recording (`Ctrl+\`, or `Ctrl+i` on older
builds). [`slidev-addon-asciinema`](https://github.com/murilo-cunha/slidev-addon-asciinema)
embeds a cast as `<Asciinema src="casts/x.cast" :playerProps="{ pauseOnMarkers: true }"/>`;
`pauseOnMarkers` makes the player stop at each marker so the presenter talks, then resumes.

```
record-casts.sh A/B/C/D ─▶ public/casts/*.cast ─▶ slides.md (Asciinema, pauseOnMarkers)
                                                 └─▶ pnpm dev (present) / pnpm build (static)
```

## Prerequisites

* `asciinema` (`brew install asciinema`); optional `agg` (`brew install agg`) to preview a
  cast as GIF. Pre-build the CLI so compile time never leaks into a recording.
* The deck is a **standalone** project (deliberately not in the pnpm workspace, to keep the
  root lockfile clean): `pnpm install --ignore-workspace --dir tools/demo/presentation` once
  (the `--ignore-workspace` flag is required — otherwise pnpm resolves to the monorepo root).

## 1. Record the casts (the user drives the terminal live)

This is interactive and belongs to the user. Tell them to run, dropping a marker at each
beat boundary (see [`presentation/RECORDING.md`](../../../tools/demo/presentation/RECORDING.md)
for the per-beat keystroke cheat-sheet and the clean-env checklist):

```bash
tools/demo/presentation/record-casts.sh A   # find & inspect (TUI)  → public/casts/A-find.cast
tools/demo/presentation/record-casts.sh B   # name a new token (TUI) → public/casts/B-name.cast
tools/demo/presentation/record-casts.sh C   # deterministic suggest (CLI) → public/casts/C-suggest.cast
```

Committed `*.cast` files are placeholders so the deck renders out of the box — re-record to
replace them. If recording markers live is awkward, record straight through and post-edit
the `.cast` to insert `[t, "m", "label"]` lines, or pass `markers` timestamps in `playerProps`.

## 2. Record the agent cast (Claude Code + design-data MCP)

The agent beat (Demo D) is now an asciinema cast like A/B/C — all four movements are
terminal recordings:

```bash
tools/demo/presentation/record-casts.sh D   # → public/casts/D-agent.cast
```

Before recording: add the `design-data` MCP server to `.mcp.json`, pre-warm with
`npx -y @adobe/design-data-agent-mcp --help`, then launch Claude Code once to approve the
connection. See [`presentation/RECORDING.md`](../../../tools/demo/presentation/RECORDING.md)
(Demo D section) for the full checklist, D1–D4 beat table, and non-determinism guidance.
The verbatim prompt is in [`tools/demo/agent-questions.md`](../../../tools/demo/agent-questions.md).

`.mcp.json` config to add:

```json
"design-data": {
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["-y", "@adobe/design-data-agent-mcp"],
  "env": {
    "DESIGN_DATA_BIN": "${PWD}/sdk/target/release/design-data",
    "DESIGN_DATA_PATH": "packages/design-data/tokens",
    "DESIGN_DATA_COMPONENTS": "packages/design-data/components"
  }
}
```

## 3. Author / edit the deck and present

Edit [`slides.md`](../../../tools/demo/presentation/slides.md): one section per demo
(find → name → AI), each beat slide embeds a cast with `pauseOnMarkers: true` and pins
`cols: 120, rows: 36`; narration goes in `<!-- ... -->` presenter notes.

```bash
moon run demo:present          # live dev server — screen-share and narrate
moon run demo:present-build    # static export to presentation/dist/
```

## Presentation gotchas

* `pauseOnMarkers` needs markers actually present in the cast — verify with playback.
* Slidev PDF/PPTX export bakes video as a poster frame; present from the live dev server or
  the static build, not a PDF.
* Be honest on screen: `query`/`resolve`/`describe`/`validate` and `suggest` are
  **deterministic** (Jaccard ranking), not a model. The agent in the recorded video is the
  only model layer. `sdk/cli/README.md` overstates `suggest` as "AI" — don't repeat that.
* The TUI `/` fuzzy-find palette is not wired up yet — drive search with `:query` / `:find`.

# Docs voice & tone (Spectrum-adapted)

Source: Spectrum Voice and Tone Framework, Adobe Design
(spectrum.adobe.com/page/voice-and-tone), Spectrum 2 alignment.

That framework governs **in-product, authenticated UI strings** — buttons, errors,
onboarding. This repo's docs (articles, `/spec/` pages, READMEs, CLI help prose) are
public reference/marketing-adjacent content, not in-product strings, so treat the four
voice principles below as a prose-review lens, not a literal rule (there's no "tone
variant by moment" here — that part of the framework doesn't apply to docs).

## The four voice principles

**Clear** — direct, not buried. One idea per sentence. No jargon left unexplained, no
action buried three clauses in.

* Do: "The `export` command emits the whole dataset as one DTCG document."
* Don't: "The `export` functionality has been designed to facilitate the retrieval of
  the complete resolved token dataset in DTCG-conformant form."

**Genuine** — honest, not performed. No marketing verbs, no claimed enthusiasm, no
significance-inflation about what a change means.

* Do: "This fixes a stale token reference in the article."
* Don't: "This exciting update ensures our documentation stays cutting-edge."

**Concise** — necessary, not more. No padding, no redundant restatement, no hedging
qualifiers that add nothing.

* Do: "Every example below is a real token you can look up on the Tokens page."
* Don't: "It's worth noting that, in general, most of the examples below tend to be
  real tokens that you can typically look up."

**Upfront** — actor and limit disclosed, not implied. Say what's still in progress,
what's provisional, what changed and why, rather than letting a reader assume.

* Do: "The Design Data Specification is still in development; the legacy format keeps
  shipping in the meantime."
* Don't: silently describing a future-state format as if it's already the one people
  should use today.

## How to apply this in review

1. Read the doc once for content correctness first (that's a separate pass — see
   accuracy review conventions elsewhere in this repo). This skill is voice/tone only.
2. Run `humanizer` first if the doc hasn't already been through it — this skill assumes
   AI-writing tells (em dashes, testament/pivotal/showcase, inline-header lists, etc.)
   are already gone. Don't re-litigate those here.
3. Walk the four principles in order (Clear → Genuine → Concise → Upfront) and flag
   violations with the specific line and which principle it breaks. Don't rewrite
   wholesale — this is a targeted pass on top of otherwise-good prose.

# Enhance sync PR (Tokens Studio → spectrum-design-data)

## When this applies

* PR opened by `mrcjhicks` from `tokens-sync/patch-spectrum2-from-main` (or similar sync branch).
* Body links to `github.com/adobe/spectrum-tokens-studio-data/actions/runs/…`.
* CI red after sync (validation, snapshot, component props, wireframe, etc.).
* Changeset missing; title still `feat: updates from spectrum-tokens-studio-data` or duplicated `feat: Feat:`.

## Repo and tools

* **Monorepo root:** workspace root (`spectrum-design-data`).
* **Changeset generator:** [`tools/token-changeset-generator`](../../../tools/token-changeset-generator) — fetches source PR motivation, runs `tdiff`, infers semver bump.
* **Automation:** [`.github/workflows/enhance-sync-pr.yml`](../../../.github/workflows/enhance-sync-pr.yml) and [`.github/actions/extract-source-pr-info`](../../../.github/actions/extract-source-pr-info).

## 1. Resolve source PR

From the design-data PR body, take the **spectrum-tokens-studio-data** Actions run URL or the **Tokens Studio PR** link.

```bash
gh pr view <N> --repo adobe/spectrum-design-data --json body,title,headRefName,url
```

If only the run URL exists, resolve merged PR from that run (same logic as `extract-source-pr-info`).

Record:

* Source PR URL (e.g. `https://github.com/adobe/spectrum-tokens-studio-data/pull/297`)
* Source author (`user.login` from that PR) for attribution

```bash
gh api repos/adobe/spectrum-tokens-studio-data/pulls/<num> --jq '{title, author: .user.login, body}'
```

## 2. Diagnose CI (suggest fixes; user approves edits)

Check out the PR branch with full history (`fetch-depth: 0`) so `tdiff` can compare to `main`.

Run in order:

```bash
moon run tokens:validateDesignData
moon run tokens:verifyDesignDataSnapshot
cd packages/tokens && pnpm ava
```

Or full graph: `moon ci` (same as GitHub Actions).

### Failure map (what to suggest)

| Symptom                                        | Likely cause                                                                                                | Suggestion                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |   |   |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | - | - |
| `checkComponentProps` lists token names        | Missing or wrong `component` on entries in `color-component.json`, `layout-component.json`, or `icons.json` | Set `component` to match token name prefix (see [`packages/tokens/test/checkComponentProps.js`](../../../packages/tokens/test/checkComponentProps.js)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |   |   |
| Schema / `color-set` errors                    | `sets` missing `light`, `dark`, or **`wireframe`**                                                          | Align with [`schemas/token-types/color-set.json`](../../../packages/tokens/schemas/token-types/color-set.json).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |   |   |
| `verifyDesignDataSnapshot` / snapshot mismatch | Validation report changed vs golden file                                                                    | Paths in the snapshot are relative to `packages/tokens/`. After `moon run sdk:build`, run **`migrate snapshot` from `packages/tokens/`** so paths match `moon run tokens:verifyDesignDataSnapshot`: `cd packages/tokens && ../../sdk/target/debug/design-data migrate snapshot ./src --output ./snapshots/validation-snapshot.json --schema-path ./schemas --exceptions-path ../design-data/naming-exceptions.json`. |   |   |
| Token file / `$schema` / `uuid`                | Invalid token shape                                                                                         | Fix per [`token-file.json`](../../../packages/tokens/schemas/token-file.json) and failing AVA tests.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |   |   |
| Alias / renamed / manifest                     | Broken refs or manifest drift                                                                               | Fix aliases; run `moon run tokens:buildManifest`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |   |   |
| Changeset lint on PR                           | Bad frontmatter                                                                                             | Valid `---` / `"@adobe/spectrum-tokens": patch \| minor \| major` / body.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |   |   |

Re-run targeted tasks after each fix until green.

## 3. PR title and body

* **Title:** One conventional prefix. Strip a leading `feat:` / `Feat:` (and similar) from the **source** title, then use `feat: <clean title>` (avoid `feat: Feat: …`).
* **Body template:**

```markdown
## Token updates from Spectrum Tokens Studio Data

**Original implementer:** @<github-login>

**Source PR:** [#<n> <title>](<url>)

**Automated sync via:** [GitHub Actions run](<run-url>)

### Source description

<paste or summarize source PR body / motivation>

---

<keep existing automated footer if present>
```

Use `gh pr edit <N> --repo adobe/spectrum-design-data --title "..." --body-file body.md`.

## 4. Changeset + git attribution

Generate changeset (requires `GITHUB_TOKEN` for API rate limits):

```bash
cd tools/token-changeset-generator && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
GITHUB_TOKEN=... node src/cli.js generate \
  --tokens-studio-pr 'https://github.com/adobe/spectrum-tokens-studio-data/pull/<num>' \
  --spectrum-tokens-pr 'https://github.com/adobe/spectrum-design-data/pull/<N>' \
  --source-author '<login>'
```

Bump type is inferred from diff (e.g. deletions → major, additions → minor).

Commit using the **source implementer’s** git identity so changelog "Thanks @…" matches design work:

```bash
git config user.email '<email>'
git config user.name '<display name>'
git add .changeset/*.md
git commit -m "chore: add changeset for <short summary>" -m "Co-authored-by: <name> <email>"
```

If the commit author is already the implementer, `Co-authored-by` is optional but harmless.

## 5. Verify

```bash
moon run tokens:validateDesignData
moon run tokens:verifyDesignDataSnapshot
cd packages/tokens && pnpm ava
pnpm changeset-lint check .changeset/*.md
```

Push the branch; confirm CI and changeset-bot on the PR.

## Reference: prior manual PRs

Well-formed examples: merged sync PRs with `token-changeset-generator`-style changesets and enriched bodies (e.g. [#615](https://github.com/adobe/spectrum-design-data/issues/615), [#593](https://github.com/adobe/spectrum-design-data/issues/593)). Early PRs used hand-written "Design motivation" + "Token diff" in the changeset body — the generator now standardizes that shape.

# Spectrum diagrams for docs articles

Turns a real technical structure (code, tokens, spec, pipeline) into a diagram that looks
like it belongs next to Spectrum's own docs, and embeds it in an article.

This skill is a **workflow on top of** the Figma MCP's own skills — it doesn't
re-document their tool mechanics. Load those when this skill tells you to.

## When to use this

* An article has an `<!-- Illustration: ... -->` placeholder comment for a diagram
  (the established convention in this repo — see `understanding-spectrum-tokens.md`).
* Someone asks for an architecture diagram, flowchart, pipeline, or tiered/cascade
  diagram to go in a `docs/site/src/articles/*.md` file.

**Not for:** decorative hero illustrations or brand illustration (bell/cloud/lightbulb
style icons). Those come from the real S2 Illustrations Figma library, not
`generate_diagram` — see [Illustration guardrails](#illustration-guardrails) below. If a
placeholder asks for one, say so and point at the library rather than faking one with
`generate_diagram`.

## Workflow

### 1. Gather the real structure first

Read the actual code, tokens, or spec the diagram represents before writing any Mermaid.
Don't invent services, edges, or tiers to "round out" a diagram — a partial, accurate
diagram beats a polished, hallucinated one. If the article prose already describes the
structure (tables, code blocks), that prose is the source of truth; walk it node by node.

### 2. Load `/figma-generate-diagram` and pick the type

This is **mandatory before calling `generate_diagram`** (per the Figma MCP server's own
instructions). It routes you to type-specific guidance and sets universal Mermaid
constraints (no emojis, no `\n` in labels, reserved words, etc.) — follow it, don't
duplicate it here.

Two shapes come up repeatedly in this repo's articles:

* **Real software architecture** (services, datastores, queues, external calls) →
  the *architecture* layout: `flowchart LR`, every node inside one of the fixed subgraphs
  (`client`/`gateway`/`service`/`datastore`/`external`/`async`), pass
  `useArchitectureLayoutCode: "FIGMA_DIAGRAM_2026"`.
* **Conceptual structure** (token tiers, a cascade/precedence model, a pipeline of
  stages) → a plain `flowchart` (see the Figma skill's `flowchart.md` reference). No
  subgraph-ID constraint applies here — use whatever grouping reads clearly.

### 3. Generate

Call `generate_diagram`. If you're iterating on the same diagram, or adding a second
diagram that should live beside the first, pass the same `fileKey` instead of creating a
new draft file each time (the Figma skill covers this).

### 4. Spectrum-aligned recolor pass (do this — it's why this skill exists)

`generate_diagram` auto-assigns colors that aren't Spectrum's, and the FigJam board
can't have its font changed to Adobe Clean. Close the color gap (font is an accepted
limitation of this output path — leave it):

1. Load `/figma-use-figjam` (FigJam-specific `use_figma` guidance) — mandatory before
   editing FigJam nodes. It documents FigJam's **coordinated shape presets**
   (`figjam-colors.md`): each `shape-with-text` node takes a fill+stroke+text triad from
   a fixed palette, not arbitrary hex — an off-palette color renders as "custom" in the
   FigJam UI and can't be re-picked from the swatch picker.
2. Read `references/spectrum-brand.md` for the mapping from Spectrum's semantic intent
   (neutral/raw, structural, accent/emphasis, final-result) onto the closest FigJam
   preset — this skill does **not** inject raw Spectrum hex into FigJam shapes.
3. Read `references/diagram-house-style.md` for the *composition* rules on top of those
   presets — which node gets the accent (and why), how to show precedence without a
   color-per-stage, when to drop repetitive edge labels, and layout/caption discipline.
   This is what keeps diagrams from reading as default-tinted flowcharts.
4. Call `get_figjam` first to get real node IDs (don't guess — `use_figma`'s `console.log`
   isn't returned, only the `return` value is).
5. Use `use_figma` to set `shape.fills`/`shape.strokes`/`shape.text.fills` per node from
   the coordinated preset, and `connector.strokes` to a dark/neutral connector-palette
   color (not a bright accent — connectors should recede). Never `figma.createPage` in
   FigJam.
6. Run the `diagram-critic` agent against the Mermaid source + a screenshot before final
   export (see `diagram-house-style.md`'s Review loop) — apply its findings in one batch.
7. Skip steps 3–6 only for a quick throwaway/exploratory diagram, not for anything going
   into a published article.

### 5. Capture

Use `get_screenshot` on the finished board (pass a high `maxDimension` — the default 1024
is too low-resolution once a board has several diagrams side by side) and save the
result to:

```
docs/site/src/assets/images/<article-slug>-<diagram-name>.png
```

(`src/assets/images/` already has a passthrough wired in `eleventy.config.js` — no build
changes needed. SVG export is preferable when FigJam's export supports it cleanly; PNG is
the fallback.)

**If several diagrams share one FigJam board/page**, `get_screenshot` only takes a
`nodeId` — there's no single node per diagram to target, so screenshot the whole page and
crop locally. Use `get_figjam` to read each node's `x`/`y`/`width`/`height` and compute a
bounding box per diagram; crop with ImageMagick (`magick board.png -crop
WxH+X+Y diagram.png`), not `sips` (`sips -c`/`--cropOffset` crops from the image
**center**, not top-left — easy to get a wrong region that silently looks plausible).
FigJam's canvas background is a light gray, not white — normalize it to match the site's
white article background: `magick diagram.png -fuzz 3% -fill white -opaque "#f5f5f5"
-trim +repage diagram.png`.

### 6. Embed in the article

Replace the `<!-- Illustration: ... -->` placeholder comment (or add a new image) with:

```md
![Alt text describing the diagram](/assets/images/<article-slug>-<diagram-name>.png)
```

Root-relative path — the site's `HtmlBasePlugin` adds the `/spectrum-design-data`
pathPrefix automatically. Write real alt text describing what the diagram shows, not the
filename.

If a diagram truly needs to be pixel-perfect on-brand (exact Spectrum token colors, no
FigJam limitations at all), the alternative is hand-authoring inline SVG directly in the
article body using `var(--spectrum-*)` custom properties (already loaded site-wide via
`@spectrum-css/tokens`). That's more effort per diagram and is the exception, not the
default path this skill optimizes for.

## Illustration guardrails

These apply whenever a diagram or the surrounding article touches actual Spectrum
illustration assets (icons like a bell, cloud, lightbulb, confetti — not
`generate_diagram` node shapes):

* **Never invent or recolor an illustration.** Pull real assets from the S2
  Illustrations Figma library (via `download_assets` / the library file) instead of
  drawing one from scratch.
* **Linear (monochrome, gray-800) is the low-attention default** — safe to use multiple
  times in one layout (e.g. several cards). Use it for routine UI/empty-state style
  callouts.
* **Gradient illustrations are high-attention** — at most one per view, never in error or
  critical-message contexts (their colors carry positive/semantic meaning that conflicts
  with error framing).
* Sizes are fixed: **S 48×48, M 96×96, L 160×160** — don't resize or restyle.

## What NOT to do

* Don't call `generate_diagram` for pie charts, mindmaps, venn diagrams, class diagrams,
  or timelines — it doesn't support them (the Figma skill lists the supported types).
* Don't skip step 4 for anything shipping in an article — an un-recolored, auto-styled
  FigJam export doesn't read as Spectrum.
* Don't regenerate more than twice on the same complaint — stop, ask what's specifically
  wrong, or suggest editing directly in FigJam.

re-document their tool mechanics. Load those when this skill tells you to.

## When to use this

* An article has an `<!-- Illustration: ... -->` placeholder comment for a diagram
  (the established convention in this repo — see `understanding-spectrum-tokens.md`).
* Someone asks for an architecture diagram, flowchart, pipeline, or tiered/cascade
  diagram to go in a `docs/site/src/articles/*.md` file.

**Not for:** decorative hero illustrations or brand illustration (bell/cloud/lightbulb
style icons). Those come from the real S2 Illustrations Figma library, not
`generate_diagram` — see [Illustration guardrails](#illustration-guardrails) below. If a
placeholder asks for one, say so and point at the library rather than faking one with
`generate_diagram`.

## Workflow

### 1. Gather the real structure first

Read the actual code, tokens, or spec the diagram represents before writing any Mermaid.
Don't invent services, edges, or tiers to "round out" a diagram — a partial, accurate
diagram beats a polished, hallucinated one. If the article prose already describes the
structure (tables, code blocks), that prose is the source of truth; walk it node by node.

### 2. Load `/figma-generate-diagram` and pick the type

This is **mandatory before calling `generate_diagram`** (per the Figma MCP server's own
instructions). It routes you to type-specific guidance and sets universal Mermaid
constraints (no emojis, no `\n` in labels, reserved words, etc.) — follow it, don't
duplicate it here.

Two shapes come up repeatedly in this repo's articles:

* **Real software architecture** (services, datastores, queues, external calls) →
  the *architecture* layout: `flowchart LR`, every node inside one of the fixed subgraphs
  (`client`/`gateway`/`service`/`datastore`/`external`/`async`), pass
  `useArchitectureLayoutCode: "FIGMA_DIAGRAM_2026"`.
* **Conceptual structure** (token tiers, a cascade/precedence model, a pipeline of
  stages) → a plain `flowchart` (see the Figma skill's `flowchart.md` reference). No
  subgraph-ID constraint applies here — use whatever grouping reads clearly.

### 3. Generate

Call `generate_diagram`. If you're iterating on the same diagram, or adding a second
diagram that should live beside the first, pass the same `fileKey` instead of creating a
new draft file each time (the Figma skill covers this).

### 4. Spectrum-aligned recolor pass (do this — it's why this skill exists)

`generate_diagram` auto-assigns colors that aren't Spectrum's, and the FigJam board
can't have its font changed to Adobe Clean. Close the color gap (font is an accepted
limitation of this output path — leave it):

1. Load `/figma-use-figjam` (FigJam-specific `use_figma` guidance) — mandatory before
   editing FigJam nodes. It documents FigJam's **coordinated shape presets**
   (`figjam-colors.md`): each `shape-with-text` node takes a fill+stroke+text triad from
   a fixed palette, not arbitrary hex — an off-palette color renders as "custom" in the
   FigJam UI and can't be re-picked from the swatch picker.
2. Read `references/spectrum-brand.md` for the mapping from Spectrum's semantic intent
   (neutral/raw, structural, accent/emphasis, final-result) onto the closest FigJam
   preset — this skill does **not** inject raw Spectrum hex into FigJam shapes.
3. Read `references/diagram-house-style.md` for the *composition* rules on top of those
   presets — which node gets the accent (and why), how to show precedence without a
   color-per-stage, when to drop repetitive edge labels, and layout/caption discipline.
   This is what keeps diagrams from reading as default-tinted flowcharts.
4. Call `get_figjam` first to get real node IDs (don't guess — `use_figma`'s `console.log`
   isn't returned, only the `return` value is).
5. Use `use_figma` to set `shape.fills`/`shape.strokes`/`shape.text.fills` per node from
   the coordinated preset, and `connector.strokes` to a dark/neutral connector-palette
   color (not a bright accent — connectors should recede). Never `figma.createPage` in
   FigJam.
6. Run the `diagram-critic` agent against the Mermaid source + a screenshot before final
   export (see `diagram-house-style.md`'s Review loop) — apply its findings in one batch.
7. Skip steps 3–6 only for a quick throwaway/exploratory diagram, not for anything going
   into a published article.

### 5. Capture

Use `get_screenshot` on the finished board (pass a high `maxDimension` — the default 1024
is too low-resolution once a board has several diagrams side by side) and save the
result to:

```
docs/site/src/assets/images/<article-slug>-<diagram-name>.png
```

(`src/assets/images/` already has a passthrough wired in `eleventy.config.js` — no build
changes needed. SVG export is preferable when FigJam's export supports it cleanly; PNG is
the fallback.)

**If several diagrams share one FigJam board/page**, `get_screenshot` only takes a
`nodeId` — there's no single node per diagram to target, so screenshot the whole page and
crop locally. Use `get_figjam` to read each node's `x`/`y`/`width`/`height` and compute a
bounding box per diagram; crop with ImageMagick (`magick board.png -crop
WxH+X+Y diagram.png`), not `sips` (`sips -c`/`--cropOffset` crops from the image
**center**, not top-left — easy to get a wrong region that silently looks plausible).
FigJam's canvas background is a light gray, not white — normalize it to match the site's
white article background: `magick diagram.png -fuzz 3% -fill white -opaque "#f5f5f5"
-trim +repage diagram.png`.

### 6. Embed in the article

Replace the `<!-- Illustration: ... -->` placeholder comment (or add a new image) with:

```md
![Alt text describing the diagram](/assets/images/<article-slug>-<diagram-name>.png)
```

Root-relative path — the site's `HtmlBasePlugin` adds the `/spectrum-design-data`
pathPrefix automatically. Write real alt text describing what the diagram shows, not the
filename.

If a diagram truly needs to be pixel-perfect on-brand (exact Spectrum token colors, no
FigJam limitations at all), the alternative is hand-authoring inline SVG directly in the
article body using `var(--spectrum-*)` custom properties (already loaded site-wide via
`@spectrum-css/tokens`). That's more effort per diagram and is the exception, not the
default path this skill optimizes for.

## Illustration guardrails

These apply whenever a diagram or the surrounding article touches actual Spectrum
illustration assets (icons like a bell, cloud, lightbulb, confetti — not
`generate_diagram` node shapes):

* **Never invent or recolor an illustration.** Pull real assets from the S2
  Illustrations Figma library (via `download_assets` / the library file) instead of
  drawing one from scratch.
* **Linear (monochrome, gray-800) is the low-attention default** — safe to use multiple
  times in one layout (e.g. several cards). Use it for routine UI/empty-state style
  callouts.
* **Gradient illustrations are high-attention** — at most one per view, never in error or
  critical-message contexts (their colors carry positive/semantic meaning that conflicts
  with error framing).
* Sizes are fixed: **S 48×48, M 96×96, L 160×160** — don't resize or restyle.

## What NOT to do

* Don't call `generate_diagram` for pie charts, mindmaps, venn diagrams, class diagrams,
  or timelines — it doesn't support them (the Figma skill lists the supported types).
* Don't skip step 4 for anything shipping in an article — an un-recolored, auto-styled
  FigJam export doesn't read as Spectrum.
* Don't regenerate more than twice on the same complaint — stop, ask what's specifically
  wrong, or suggest editing directly in FigJam.

# TUI UX review & design partnership

The `design-data` TUI (`sdk/tui`) is a ratatui/Elm-architecture terminal app for authoring
and inspecting Spectrum design tokens. This skill helps you evaluate and improve the **user
experience** — conventions, ergonomics, discoverability, workflow smoothness — using the
tuiwright MCP tools to drive and observe the app.

> **NOT correctness testing.** For regression tests and render assertions use `tui-verify`.
> This skill hands off to it whenever a finding needs a deterministic guard.

## Orientation — TUI surfaces

| Surface              | Entry key   | Source files                                                 | What it does                                                            |
| -------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Command palette**  | `:`         | `src/command.rs`, `src/update_command.rs`                    | All commands: query / resolve / describe / validate / new / find / name |
| **Fuzzy find**       | `/`         | `src/fuzzy.rs`, `src/update.rs`                              | Live-ranked token search; Esc restores prior view                       |
| **Authoring wizard** | `:new`      | `src/wizard.rs`, `src/wizard_draft.rs`, `src/wizard_common/` | 4-screen token creation: Intent → Classification → Values → Confirm     |
| **Find wizard**      | `:find`     | `src/find.rs`, `src/view_find.rs`                            | Filter by property/component/variant/state/intent                       |
| **Naming wizard**    | `:name`     | `src/naming.rs`                                              | 3-screen name assembly; copies to clipboard                             |
| **Help overlay**     | `?`         | `src/help.rs`                                                | Scrollable keybinding reference                                         |
| **Home screen**      | (default)   | `src/logo.rs`, `src/view.rs`                                 | Logo + command table                                                    |
| **List views**       | (result)    | `src/app_views.rs`, `src/view.rs`                            | query / resolve / validate result tables                                |
| **Describe view**    | `:describe` | `src/app_views.rs`, `src/view.rs`                            | Component token breakdown, scrollable                                   |
| **Theme**            | (config)    | `src/theme.rs`                                               | `terminal()` (16-color) and `spectrum()` (truecolor)                    |

**Source of truth for keybindings and commands**: always read `src/help.rs` (`HELP_TEXT`)
and the `Command` enum in `src/command.rs` before asserting what the app does — the
documentation drifts; the code does not.

***

## Drive-tier decision guide

Choose the tier that answers your question with the least friction.

```
tui_headless (NDJSON replay)   ← fast, deterministic, no PTY — default for layout & flow
tui_open + send_keys + snapshot ← real terminal interaction, mouse, truecolor
tui_record_start → tui_record_stop → tui_to_gif ← visual evidence for findings
```

### When to use each tier

| Question                                                | Use                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| "How does the palette render after submitting a query?" | `tui_headless` with NDJSON seed               |
| "What does the home screen look like at 80×24?"         | `tui_headless` (set cols/rows params)         |
| "Does Tab autocomplete feel natural while typing?"      | `tui_open` + `tui_send_keys` + `tui_snapshot` |
| "Does mouse click-to-select work on the token list?"    | `tui_open` + live interaction                 |
| "Show the full wizard workflow as evidence in a report" | Record with `tui_record_*` + `tui_to_gif`     |
| "Is the truecolor Spectrum theme rendering correctly?"  | `tui_open` + `tui_snapshot` (image mode)      |

### NDJSON message format

Each line of an NDJSON replay file is one serialized `Message`. The only format confirmed
to work reliably in headless mode is `PaletteSubmit` — it drives the TUI as if the user
typed the command and pressed Enter:

```jsonl
{"PaletteSubmit":"query property=background-color"}
{"PaletteSubmit":"describe button"}
{"PaletteSubmit":"validate"}
{"PaletteSubmit":"new accent background"}
```

> **Key events in NDJSON are unreliable.** The `{"Key":...}` format exists but does not
> reliably produce the expected state changes in headless replay — use `tui_open` +
> `tui_send_keys` for anything requiring keyboard navigation (j/k, Esc, Tab, etc.).

**Ready-made seeds for this repo** live in the tuiwright examples directory:
`/Users/garthdb/Projects/tuiwright/examples/spectrum-design-data/`
(browse.ndjson, query-background-color.ndjson, describe-button.ndjson). Use them as starting
points, then extend or truncate as needed.

### Tool quick-reference

```
tui_headless(ndjson, cols, rows, format)          → rendered text grid (+ PNG if freeze on PATH)
tui_open(cols, rows)                              → open live pane
tui_send_keys(keys)                               → send input (\r=Enter, \x1b=Esc, \x1b[A=Up, \x1b[B=Down)
tui_snapshot(format)                              → capture live pane (text | image | both)
tui_wait_for(text, timeout_ms)                    → block until text appears (server-side 5s cap — use Bash sleep for longer waits)
tui_resize(cols, rows)                            → resize live pane
tui_assert(contains, not_contains, ndjson, ...)   → pass/fail assertion on text presence
tui_diff(baseline, ndjson, create_if_missing)     → compare against a named .snap.json baseline
tui_record_start(path)                            → begin asciinema .cast recording
tui_record_stop()                                 → finalize recording
tui_to_gif(cast, gif)                             → convert .cast to GIF via agg
tui_close()                                       → kill live pane
```

> **`tui_snapshot` may hang on live panes.** If it hangs >10s, kill the session and use
> the rmux CLI fallback instead:
>
> ```bash
> rmux new-session -d -s tui-qa -x 120 -y 36 "sdk/target/release/design-data packages/design-data/tokens --components packages/design-data/components"
> sleep 2
> rmux send-keys -t tui-qa "query property=background-color" Enter
> sleep 1
> rmux capture-pane -t tui-qa -p
> ```

`tuiwright.toml` (repo root) configures launch (`sdk/target/release/design-data`), default
size (120×36), and the headless\_snapshot command template.

***

## Workflow 1 — QA / UX review pass

Use when asked to review a surface or the full TUI for UX quality.

### Step 0 — Build and verify the binary

Always do this before any QA session. A stale binary silently produces wrong behavior and
wrong help content.

```bash
# Check whether the binary is older than key source files:
ls -la sdk/target/release/design-data
find sdk/tui/src -newer sdk/target/release/design-data -name "*.rs"

# If any source files are newer, rebuild:
cargo build -p design-data-cli --release
# or: moon run :build
```

Also verify the `?` help overlay matches `src/help.rs` — run a headless probe with
`{"PaletteSubmit":""}` (home screen), then check if the binary's live help overlay content
matches what `help.rs` says. If they differ, rebuild before proceeding.

### Step 1 — Define scope

Pick one surface (e.g. "the command palette") or state "full end-to-end pass." Write it down
before driving.

### Step 2 — Read the source of truth

```bash
# Check the actual keybindings:
# Read sdk/tui/src/help.rs   (HELP_TEXT constant)
# Read sdk/tui/src/command.rs  (Command enum + define_commands! macro)
```

Do this even for surfaces you think you know — implementations drift.

### Step 3 — Drive and observe

For each surface in scope, use the tier decision guide above. Drive a representative user
journey through the surface (happy path, then edge cases: empty input, Esc mid-flow, invalid
input, very long content, narrow terminal).

Take a `tui_snapshot` or `tui_headless` result at each key state. Note: what rendered, what
was expected from convention, any gap.

Use `tui_resize` to check graceful degradation at 120×36 (target), 80×24 (standard), and
narrow/short sizes. The logo drops below 33 content rows — verify that still works.

### Step 4 — Evaluate against conventions

Open [`references/tui-conventions.md`](references/tui-conventions.md) and step through the
checklist for each surface you drove. Mark each convention: ✓ match / \~ partial / ✗ gap.

### Step 5 — Evaluate against heuristics

Open [`references/qa-playbook.md`](references/qa-playbook.md) and run the heuristic checklist.
For each failing heuristic, note the surface, the exact gap, and a severity:

* **Blocker** — prevents a user goal or causes confusion about state
* **Friction** — works, but harder than it should be; user has to figure it out
* **Polish** — works fine, small improvement opportunity

### Step 6 — Capture evidence

For each finding that benefits from visual evidence:

```
# GIF of a workflow
tui_record_start("/tmp/finding-N.cast")
# … drive the flow with tui_open / tui_send_keys / tui_snapshot …
tui_record_stop()
tui_to_gif("/tmp/finding-N.cast", "/tmp/finding-N.gif")
# Read /tmp/finding-N.gif  ← include in report
```

### Step 7 — Emit deliverables (all four)

See **Deliverables spec** below.

***

## Workflow 2 — Workflow / journey planning

Use when asked "how would a user do X?" or to identify whether a task is discoverable.

### Step 1 — State the user goal

Write it out: "User wants to author a new color token." The goal should be what the user
wants to *accomplish*, not which command to run.

### Step 2 — Map what conventions would predict

Given the goal, describe what an experienced terminal-app user would *try first* — based on
the conventions in [`references/tui-conventions.md`](references/tui-conventions.md). This is
the baseline expectation before touching the actual app.

### Step 3 — Drive the actual happy path

Drive the canonical successful path using `tui_headless` or `tui_open` + `tui_send_keys`.
Record a GIF of this path.

### Step 4 — Drive the predicted-but-wrong paths

Try the paths a user would try based on convention that the app does NOT support (if any).
Document what happens (error? silence? wrong result? accidental navigation?).

### Step 5 — Identify discoverability gaps

* Are the entry points for this goal visible on the home screen or reachable from `?`?
* Does the command autocomplete surface it?
* Does partial input give helpful feedback?
* Would a user arriving at the wrong screen understand how to correct?

### Step 6 — Deliver

Write a journey map (goal → steps → what the user sees at each step → where they could
get stuck) plus findings for each gap, using the Deliverables spec below.

***

## Workflow 3 — QoL recommendation

Use when asked "how can we improve X?" or after a review pass surfaces specific friction.

### Step 1 — Categorize the improvement

* **Quick win**: a text change (empty-state copy, footer hint, error message), a single
  keybinding alias, or a minor layout tweak. Can be a direct inline edit.
* **Larger change**: new mode, new command, new wizard screen, significant interaction
  redesign. File a beads issue instead of inline-editing.

### Step 2 — For quick wins — verify the guardrails apply

Before proposing an edit, check the architectural guardrails:

* `tests/budget.rs` enforces 800-LOC cap per `src/` file — check `wc -l` on the target.
* No `async` in `view*.rs` (the no-async-in-render rule).
* `Message` variants must be ≤128 bytes (box large payloads if needed).
* Adding or renaming a command requires updating *both* `command.rs` *and* the `COMMANDS`
  constant in `src/logo.rs` (a bidirectional sync test guards this; it will fail if out of sync).
* Adding a hit region requires keeping `compute_hit_regions` in sync with `view::draw`
  (runtime.rs and tests guard this too).

After any inline fix, note: "run `cargo test -p design-data-tui` to verify guardrails pass."

### Step 3 — Deliver

Inline edit + explanation for quick wins. Beads issue with design rationale for larger changes.
Use the Deliverables spec below.

***

## Deliverables spec

Every review or recommendation produces some or all of these four artifacts.

### 1. Structured critique report

```markdown
## TUI UX Review — [scope] — [date]

**Method:** [headless / live / mixed] — [why that tier]

### Summary
[2–4 sentence overall verdict]

### Findings

#### [Surface name]

| # | Severity | Finding | Convention | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Friction | Esc in the naming wizard cancels all three screens at once | Esc should undo one step at a time (lazygit, helix) | Add per-screen cancel that pops to prior screen |

**Evidence:** [inline snapshot text or GIF path]

### Triage table
| Finding | Beads ID | Inline fix | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
```

### 2. Beads issues

For each Blocker or Friction finding:

```bash
bd create \
  --type=bug \   # or feature for improvements
  --title="[Surface]: [one-line description]" \
  --description="## Problem
[What happens and why it's wrong/suboptimal]

## Convention / expected behavior
[What users expect based on analogous TUIs — cite references/tui-conventions.md]

## Repro
[NDJSON seed or tui_send_keys sequence that demonstrates the issue]

## Suggested fix
[Concrete recommendation, with file:line reference if known]" \
  --priority=2   # 1 for Blocker, 2 for Friction, 3 for Polish
```

### 3. Inline fix proposals

For quick wins, propose the edit using the Edit tool with:

* File path + old\_string / new\_string
* One-sentence rationale
* Note: "verify with `cargo test -p design-data-tui`"

### 4. Annotated GIFs / screenshots

Capture evidence using the record workflow in Step 6 of Workflow 1. Read the resulting GIF
into the conversation to annotate it (describe what to look for, circle attention areas in
the report text).

***

## Handoff to tui-verify

When a finding needs a correctness assertion or a regression guard — "does this cell render
the right symbol?", "does this layout hold at 80×24?" — stop and use `tui-verify` instead.
Do **not** invent a buffer assertion inline; let `tui-verify`'s Tier 1 handle it.

```
For correctness tests → tui-verify (Tier 1 buffer assertions, tui_assert, tui_diff)
For UX/product judgment → tui-ux (this skill)
```

***

## Gotchas

* **Build the binary first — and check for staleness.** `tuiwright.toml` points at
  `sdk/target/release/design-data`. A stale binary silently shows old behavior and old
  help text. Run `find sdk/tui/src -newer sdk/target/release/design-data -name "*.rs"` —
  if anything is newer, rebuild with `cargo build -p design-data-cli --release`.
* **TOML scoping in tuiwright.toml.** Top-level keys (like `headless_snapshot`) must appear
  *before* the first `[section]` header in the file. A key after `[size]` becomes
  `size.headless_snapshot` (silently ignored) rather than the root `headless_snapshot`.
* **`tui_snapshot` may hang.** The tuiwright SDK's rmux connection can fail to capture live
  panes even when `tui_open` reports success. If `tui_snapshot` hangs >10s, use the rmux
  CLI fallback (see Tool quick-reference above).
* **`tui_wait_for` has a server-side 5s cap.** The `timeout_ms` parameter is capped at
  5000ms by the server regardless of the value you pass. For operations that take longer,
  use `Bash: sleep N` after sending the command.
* **800-LOC cap.** `tests/budget.rs` rejects `src/` files over 800 lines. Check `wc -l` on
  any file you're about to touch.
* **No async in view.** `tests/budget.rs` scans `view*.rs` for `async fn` and fails the
  build. All render code must be synchronous.
* **Message size budget.** Every `Message` variant must be ≤128 bytes. Box large payloads
  (see `DescribeDone`, `ValidateDone` as examples).
* **Command ↔ home-screen sync.** The `COMMANDS` constant in `src/logo.rs` must stay in
  sync with the `Command` enum. A bidirectional sync test enforces this.
* **Hit-region ↔ layout sync.** `compute_hit_regions` in `runtime.rs` must match `view::draw`.
  A test in `runtime.rs` guards this; it will catch any drift.
* **`--no-resume-wizard` for clean state.** When driving the wizard from a fresh state,
  pass `--no-resume-wizard` via args in `tuiwright.toml` or the `tui_open` `args` param to
  avoid picking up a persisted draft from a prior session.

| **Theme**            | (config)    | `src/theme.rs`                                               | `terminal()` (16-color) and `spectrum()` (truecolor)                    |

**Source of truth for keybindings and commands**: always read `src/help.rs` (`HELP_TEXT`)
and the `Command` enum in `src/command.rs` before asserting what the app does — the
documentation drifts; the code does not.

***

## Drive-tier decision guide

Choose the tier that answers your question with the least friction.

```
tui_headless (NDJSON replay)   ← fast, deterministic, no PTY — default for layout & flow
tui_open + send_keys + snapshot ← real terminal interaction, mouse, truecolor
tui_record_start → tui_record_stop → tui_to_gif ← visual evidence for findings
```

### When to use each tier

| Question                                                | Use                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| "How does the palette render after submitting a query?" | `tui_headless` with NDJSON seed               |
| "What does the home screen look like at 80×24?"         | `tui_headless` (set cols/rows params)         |
| "Does Tab autocomplete feel natural while typing?"      | `tui_open` + `tui_send_keys` + `tui_snapshot` |
| "Does mouse click-to-select work on the token list?"    | `tui_open` + live interaction                 |
| "Show the full wizard workflow as evidence in a report" | Record with `tui_record_*` + `tui_to_gif`     |
| "Is the truecolor Spectrum theme rendering correctly?"  | `tui_open` + `tui_snapshot` (image mode)      |

### NDJSON message format

Each line of an NDJSON replay file is one serialized `Message`. The only format confirmed
to work reliably in headless mode is `PaletteSubmit` — it drives the TUI as if the user
typed the command and pressed Enter:

```jsonl
{"PaletteSubmit":"query property=background-color"}
{"PaletteSubmit":"describe button"}
{"PaletteSubmit":"validate"}
{"PaletteSubmit":"new accent background"}
```

> **Key events in NDJSON are unreliable.** The `{"Key":...}` format exists but does not
> reliably produce the expected state changes in headless replay — use `tui_open` +
> `tui_send_keys` for anything requiring keyboard navigation (j/k, Esc, Tab, etc.).

**Ready-made seeds for this repo** live in the tuiwright examples directory:
`/Users/garthdb/Projects/tuiwright/examples/spectrum-design-data/`
(browse.ndjson, query-background-color.ndjson, describe-button.ndjson). Use them as starting
points, then extend or truncate as needed.

### Tool quick-reference

```
tui_headless(ndjson, cols, rows, format)          → rendered text grid (+ PNG if freeze on PATH)
tui_open(cols, rows)                              → open live pane
tui_send_keys(keys)                               → send input (\r=Enter, \x1b=Esc, \x1b[A=Up, \x1b[B=Down)
tui_snapshot(format)                              → capture live pane (text | image | both)
tui_wait_for(text, timeout_ms)                    → block until text appears (server-side 5s cap — use Bash sleep for longer waits)
tui_resize(cols, rows)                            → resize live pane
tui_assert(contains, not_contains, ndjson, ...)   → pass/fail assertion on text presence
tui_diff(baseline, ndjson, create_if_missing)     → compare against a named .snap.json baseline
tui_record_start(path)                            → begin asciinema .cast recording
tui_record_stop()                                 → finalize recording
tui_to_gif(cast, gif)                             → convert .cast to GIF via agg
tui_close()                                       → kill live pane
```

> **`tui_snapshot` may hang on live panes.** If it hangs >10s, kill the session and use
> the rmux CLI fallback instead:
>
> ```bash
> rmux new-session -d -s tui-qa -x 120 -y 36 "sdk/target/release/design-data packages/design-data/tokens --components packages/design-data/components"
> sleep 2
> rmux send-keys -t tui-qa "query property=background-color" Enter
> sleep 1
> rmux capture-pane -t tui-qa -p
> ```

`tuiwright.toml` (repo root) configures launch (`sdk/target/release/design-data`), default
size (120×36), and the headless\_snapshot command template.

***

## Workflow 1 — QA / UX review pass

Use when asked to review a surface or the full TUI for UX quality.

### Step 0 — Build and verify the binary

Always do this before any QA session. A stale binary silently produces wrong behavior and
wrong help content.

```bash
# Check whether the binary is older than key source files:
ls -la sdk/target/release/design-data
find sdk/tui/src -newer sdk/target/release/design-data -name "*.rs"

# If any source files are newer, rebuild:
cargo build -p design-data-cli --release
# or: moon run :build
```

Also verify the `?` help overlay matches `src/help.rs` — run a headless probe with
`{"PaletteSubmit":""}` (home screen), then check if the binary's live help overlay content
matches what `help.rs` says. If they differ, rebuild before proceeding.

### Step 1 — Define scope

Pick one surface (e.g. "the command palette") or state "full end-to-end pass." Write it down
before driving.

### Step 2 — Read the source of truth

```bash
# Check the actual keybindings:
# Read sdk/tui/src/help.rs   (HELP_TEXT constant)
# Read sdk/tui/src/command.rs  (Command enum + define_commands! macro)
```

Do this even for surfaces you think you know — implementations drift.

### Step 3 — Drive and observe

For each surface in scope, use the tier decision guide above. Drive a representative user
journey through the surface (happy path, then edge cases: empty input, Esc mid-flow, invalid
input, very long content, narrow terminal).

Take a `tui_snapshot` or `tui_headless` result at each key state. Note: what rendered, what
was expected from convention, any gap.

Use `tui_resize` to check graceful degradation at 120×36 (target), 80×24 (standard), and
narrow/short sizes. The logo drops below 33 content rows — verify that still works.

### Step 4 — Evaluate against conventions

Open [`references/tui-conventions.md`](references/tui-conventions.md) and step through the
checklist for each surface you drove. Mark each convention: ✓ match / \~ partial / ✗ gap.

### Step 5 — Evaluate against heuristics

Open [`references/qa-playbook.md`](references/qa-playbook.md) and run the heuristic checklist.
For each failing heuristic, note the surface, the exact gap, and a severity:

* **Blocker** — prevents a user goal or causes confusion about state
* **Friction** — works, but harder than it should be; user has to figure it out
* **Polish** — works fine, small improvement opportunity

### Step 6 — Capture evidence

For each finding that benefits from visual evidence:

```
# GIF of a workflow
tui_record_start("/tmp/finding-N.cast")
# … drive the flow with tui_open / tui_send_keys / tui_snapshot …
tui_record_stop()
tui_to_gif("/tmp/finding-N.cast", "/tmp/finding-N.gif")
# Read /tmp/finding-N.gif  ← include in report
```

### Step 7 — Emit deliverables (all four)

See **Deliverables spec** below.

***

## Workflow 2 — Workflow / journey planning

Use when asked "how would a user do X?" or to identify whether a task is discoverable.

### Step 1 — State the user goal

Write it out: "User wants to author a new color token." The goal should be what the user
wants to *accomplish*, not which command to run.

### Step 2 — Map what conventions would predict

Given the goal, describe what an experienced terminal-app user would *try first* — based on
the conventions in [`references/tui-conventions.md`](references/tui-conventions.md). This is
the baseline expectation before touching the actual app.

### Step 3 — Drive the actual happy path

Drive the canonical successful path using `tui_headless` or `tui_open` + `tui_send_keys`.
Record a GIF of this path.

### Step 4 — Drive the predicted-but-wrong paths

Try the paths a user would try based on convention that the app does NOT support (if any).
Document what happens (error? silence? wrong result? accidental navigation?).

### Step 5 — Identify discoverability gaps

* Are the entry points for this goal visible on the home screen or reachable from `?`?
* Does the command autocomplete surface it?
* Does partial input give helpful feedback?
* Would a user arriving at the wrong screen understand how to correct?

### Step 6 — Deliver

Write a journey map (goal → steps → what the user sees at each step → where they could
get stuck) plus findings for each gap, using the Deliverables spec below.

***

## Workflow 3 — QoL recommendation

Use when asked "how can we improve X?" or after a review pass surfaces specific friction.

### Step 1 — Categorize the improvement

* **Quick win**: a text change (empty-state copy, footer hint, error message), a single
  keybinding alias, or a minor layout tweak. Can be a direct inline edit.
* **Larger change**: new mode, new command, new wizard screen, significant interaction
  redesign. File a beads issue instead of inline-editing.

### Step 2 — For quick wins — verify the guardrails apply

Before proposing an edit, check the architectural guardrails:

* `tests/budget.rs` enforces 800-LOC cap per `src/` file — check `wc -l` on the target.
* No `async` in `view*.rs` (the no-async-in-render rule).
* `Message` variants must be ≤128 bytes (box large payloads if needed).
* Adding or renaming a command requires updating *both* `command.rs` *and* the `COMMANDS`
  constant in `src/logo.rs` (a bidirectional sync test guards this; it will fail if out of sync).
* Adding a hit region requires keeping `compute_hit_regions` in sync with `view::draw`
  (runtime.rs and tests guard this too).

After any inline fix, note: "run `cargo test -p design-data-tui` to verify guardrails pass."

### Step 3 — Deliver

Inline edit + explanation for quick wins. Beads issue with design rationale for larger changes.
Use the Deliverables spec below.

***

## Deliverables spec

Every review or recommendation produces some or all of these four artifacts.

### 1. Structured critique report

```markdown
## TUI UX Review — [scope] — [date]

**Method:** [headless / live / mixed] — [why that tier]

### Summary
[2–4 sentence overall verdict]

### Findings

#### [Surface name]

| # | Severity | Finding | Convention | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Friction | Esc in the naming wizard cancels all three screens at once | Esc should undo one step at a time (lazygit, helix) | Add per-screen cancel that pops to prior screen |

**Evidence:** [inline snapshot text or GIF path]

### Triage table
| Finding | Beads ID | Inline fix | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
```

### 2. Beads issues

For each Blocker or Friction finding:

```bash
bd create \
  --type=bug \   # or feature for improvements
  --title="[Surface]: [one-line description]" \
  --description="## Problem
[What happens and why it's wrong/suboptimal]

## Convention / expected behavior
[What users expect based on analogous TUIs — cite references/tui-conventions.md]

## Repro
[NDJSON seed or tui_send_keys sequence that demonstrates the issue]

## Suggested fix
[Concrete recommendation, with file:line reference if known]" \
  --priority=2   # 1 for Blocker, 2 for Friction, 3 for Polish
```

### 3. Inline fix proposals

For quick wins, propose the edit using the Edit tool with:

* File path + old\_string / new\_string
* One-sentence rationale
* Note: "verify with `cargo test -p design-data-tui`"

### 4. Annotated GIFs / screenshots

Capture evidence using the record workflow in Step 6 of Workflow 1. Read the resulting GIF
into the conversation to annotate it (describe what to look for, circle attention areas in
the report text).

***

## Handoff to tui-verify

When a finding needs a correctness assertion or a regression guard — "does this cell render
the right symbol?", "does this layout hold at 80×24?" — stop and use `tui-verify` instead.
Do **not** invent a buffer assertion inline; let `tui-verify`'s Tier 1 handle it.

```
For correctness tests → tui-verify (Tier 1 buffer assertions, tui_assert, tui_diff)
For UX/product judgment → tui-ux (this skill)
```

***

## Gotchas

* **Build the binary first — and check for staleness.** `tuiwright.toml` points at
  `sdk/target/release/design-data`. A stale binary silently shows old behavior and old
  help text. Run `find sdk/tui/src -newer sdk/target/release/design-data -name "*.rs"` —
  if anything is newer, rebuild with `cargo build -p design-data-cli --release`.
* **TOML scoping in tuiwright.toml.** Top-level keys (like `headless_snapshot`) must appear
  *before* the first `[section]` header in the file. A key after `[size]` becomes
  `size.headless_snapshot` (silently ignored) rather than the root `headless_snapshot`.
* **`tui_snapshot` may hang.** The tuiwright SDK's rmux connection can fail to capture live
  panes even when `tui_open` reports success. If `tui_snapshot` hangs >10s, use the rmux
  CLI fallback (see Tool quick-reference above).
* **`tui_wait_for` has a server-side 5s cap.** The `timeout_ms` parameter is capped at
  5000ms by the server regardless of the value you pass. For operations that take longer,
  use `Bash: sleep N` after sending the command.
* **800-LOC cap.** `tests/budget.rs` rejects `src/` files over 800 lines. Check `wc -l` on
  any file you're about to touch.
* **No async in view.** `tests/budget.rs` scans `view*.rs` for `async fn` and fails the
  build. All render code must be synchronous.
* **Message size budget.** Every `Message` variant must be ≤128 bytes. Box large payloads
  (see `DescribeDone`, `ValidateDone` as examples).
* **Command ↔ home-screen sync.** The `COMMANDS` constant in `src/logo.rs` must stay in
  sync with the `Command` enum. A bidirectional sync test enforces this.
* **Hit-region ↔ layout sync.** `compute_hit_regions` in `runtime.rs` must match `view::draw`.
  A test in `runtime.rs` guards this; it will catch any drift.
* **`--no-resume-wizard` for clean state.** When driving the wizard from a fresh state,
  pass `--no-resume-wizard` via args in `tuiwright.toml` or the `tui_open` `args` param to
  avoid picking up a persisted draft from a prior session.

name: tui-verify
description: >-
  Verifies that the design-data TUI (sdk/tui) renders correctly and behaves as expected

  or Ghostty + screencapture for pixel-level fidelity. Use when asked to verify, test, or

license: Apache-2.0
compatibility: >-
  Designed for Claude Code in the spectrum-design-data repo. Tier 1 requires Rust/Cargo
  and the design-data CLI built (cargo build -p design-data-cli). Tier 2 requires rmux
  0.3.x on PATH. Tier 3 (asciinema) requires asciinema 3.x and agg on PATH. Tier 3
  (Ghostty) requires macOS, Ghostty 1.3.0+, Screen Recording TCC permission, and
  GetWindowID on PATH.
---

# TUI verification (3-tier strategy)

The `design-data` TUI (`sdk/tui`) has a purpose-built verification stack. Choose the
**lowest** tier that answers your question — Tier 1 is fastest and most exact, Tier 3 is
the only one that catches visual/glyph issues.

```
Tier 1  render_to_buffer / TestBackend  ← deterministic, no terminal, CI backbone
Tier 2  rmux + capture-pane             ← real binary, live screen text
Tier 3  asciinema + agg / Ghostty       ← pixel image for glyph/colour verification
```

## Prerequisites

* **All tiers**: `cargo build -p design-data-cli --release` (or `moon run :build`) so the
  `design-data` binary is on PATH / in `sdk/target/release/`.
* **Tier 2**: `rmux` 0.3.x on PATH (`brew install rmux`).
* **Tier 3 (asciinema)**: `asciinema` 3.x + `agg` on PATH (`brew install asciinema agg`).
* **Tier 3 (Ghostty)**: Ghostty 1.3.0+, macOS Screen Recording permission granted to the
  controlling terminal, and `GetWindowID` (`brew install smokris/getwindowid/getwindowid`).

***

## 1. Tier 1 — in-process buffer assertions (default)

`render_to_buffer(&mut model, w, h)` builds a ratatui `TestBackend` at an exact size,
draws once, and returns the `Buffer` for cell-level assertions. No terminal emulator.
All 200+ existing tests use this pattern.

**Run the full suite** (always start here):

```bash
cargo test -p design-data-tui        # or: moon run :test
```

**Add a targeted assertion** — follow the patterns in
[`references/tier1-test-api.md`](references/tier1-test-api.md)
(source: `sdk/tui/tests/render.rs`, `sdk/tui/tests/common/mod.rs`):

```rust
use common::{render_to_buffer, make_graph_with_tokens, update_ctx};

#[test]
fn my_new_feature_renders_label() {
    let graph = make_graph_with_tokens(&["accent-color"]);
    let ctx  = update_ctx(&graph);
    let mut model = Model::new();
    update(&mut model, Message::PaletteSubmit("query property=accent-color".into()), &ctx);
    let buf = render_to_buffer(&mut model, 80, 24);
    // assert specific cell or scan rows:
    assert_eq!(buf.cell((0, 0)).unwrap().symbol(), "▶");
}
```

**Layout at a specific size** — the committed breakpoints are documented in
[`references/tier1-test-api.md`](references/tier1-test-api.md#layout-breakpoints-sdktuitestslayoutrs)
(source: `sdk/tui/tests/layout.rs`):

| Size       | What to check                                                            |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `120 × 36` | Spectrum/auto-demo target — logo + all panels visible                    |
| `80 × 24`  | Standard small terminal — no overflow, table readable                    |
| `80 × 33`  | Logo present (content area = 31 rows, the exact threshold)               |
| `80 × 32`  | Logo absent — name/hint/prompt/commands still render (content = 30 rows) |
| `10 × 5`   | Narrow — should not panic                                                |
| `1 × 33`   | Very narrow at logo threshold height — should not panic                  |

***

## 2. Tier 2 — live real binary via rmux (ad-hoc verification)

Use when Tier 1 isn't enough: mouse capture, truecolor Spectrum theme, a real TTY
interaction the in-process harness can't simulate.

**Generic runner — simplest path:**

```bash
bash tools/demo/auto/verify-tui.sh \
  --dataset packages/design-data \
  --steps path/to/steps.txt
```

Step file format (one directive per line):

```
# Comments are ignored
send :
type query property=accent-color
send Enter
wait accent-color
expect accent-color
refute Error
```

Directives: `send KEY` (rmux key name), `type TEXT` (typed with 60 ms animation delay),
`literal TEXT` (send text with no key interpretation, no animation), `wait REGEX` (block
until pattern appears, 120 s timeout), `quiet [N]` (wait until pane stable for N polls),
`expect REGEX` (assert present), `refute REGEX` (assert absent), `capture` (print current
screen to stdout), `sleep N` (sleep N seconds).

The runner prints the pane contents after each `capture` or `expect`/`refute` — read those
to visually confirm layout. Exit code is 0 only when all assertions pass.

**Escape hatch — source `rmux-drive.sh` directly for a custom one-off:**

```bash
source tools/demo/auto/lib/rmux-drive.sh

start_session dd-verify "design-data packages/design-data --theme spectrum --no-resume-wizard"
wait_for dd-verify "commands" 30          # wait for home screen
send_literal dd-verify ":"
type_keys dd-verify "query property=accent-color"
send_keys dd-verify "Enter"
wait_for dd-verify "accent-color"
assert_contains dd-verify "accent-color" "token row present"
capture dd-verify                         # print for agent to read
print_summary verify
end_session dd-verify
```

See [`references/tier2-rmux-api.md`](references/tier2-rmux-api.md) for the full
helper reference (source: `tools/demo/auto/lib/rmux-drive.sh`).

**Moon task** (runs locally, not CI — rmux needs a real PTY):

```bash
moon run demo:tui-verify -- --dataset packages/design-data --steps my-steps.txt
```

***

## 3. Tier 3 — visual / pixel capture

Use only when Tier 1 can't answer the question: glyph widths, wide-char alignment,
Spectrum truecolor swatch colours, box-drawing rendering, font fallback.

**asciinema + agg (deterministic GIF — use this first):**

Record a flow inside the rmux pane (same way `auto-demo.sh` does):

```bash
source tools/demo/auto/lib/rmux-drive.sh
start_session dd-vis
# Inside the pane: wrap the binary in asciinema rec
send_keys dd-vis "asciinema rec /tmp/out.cast --cols 120 --rows 36 --overwrite -- design-data packages/design-data --theme spectrum --no-resume-wizard" Enter
wait_for dd-vis "commands" 30
send_literal dd-vis ":"
type_keys dd-vis "query property=accent-color"
send_keys dd-vis "Enter"
wait_for dd-vis "accent-color" 10
send_keys dd-vis "q"
wait_quiet dd-vis
end_session dd-vis

# Render to GIF — same agg invocation as split-cast.py uses:
agg /tmp/out.cast /tmp/out.gif --cols 120 --rows 36

# Claude can then read the GIF:
# Read tool: /tmp/out.gif
```

**Ghostty + screencapture (real-terminal pixels, macOS only):**

```bash
# 1. Open Ghostty with a pinned cell size (window-width/height are in cells):
osascript -e 'tell application "Ghostty" to activate'
# Or launch from CLI; set window-width = 120, window-height = 36 in Ghostty config.

# 2. Drive input via AppleScript:
osascript <<'EOF'
tell application "Ghostty"
  set t to focused terminal of selected tab of front window
  input text ":query property=accent-color" to t
  send key "return" to t
end tell
EOF

sleep 0.5   # let the frame render

# 3. Capture the window to PNG:
WIN_ID=$(GetWindowID Ghostty "")          # or pass partial title
screencapture -l"$WIN_ID" -o /tmp/tui.png

# Claude reads the image:
# Read tool: /tmp/tui.png
```

**Caveats for Tier 3:**

* `agg` GIF uses its own renderer/font — faithful for layout, not for "does it look exactly
  like Ghostty."
* Ghostty + `screencapture` requires Screen Recording TCC permission on the controlling
  terminal. It is **not deterministic** across machines/DPI/fonts (good on-demand spot
  check, poor committed golden).
* Images support only **fuzzy assertions** ("logo fits", "columns aligned", "swatch is
  indigo") — not cell-exact. Prefer Tier 1 for exactness.

***

## Conventions

* **asciinema, not VHS.** The `tools/demo/videos/` pipeline uses VHS for video manifests
  — do not touch it. The `tools/demo/auto/` pipeline uses asciinema — use that.
* **rmux, not tmux.** The `rmux-drive.sh` library expects `rmux` on PATH.
* The binary takes its terminal size from the real terminal (or rmux pane geometry). To
  test at a fixed size in the real binary, set the rmux pane with `RMUX_COLS`/`RMUX_ROWS`
  in `rmux-drive.sh` (default 120×36). For exact sizes in tests use `TestBackend` (Tier 1).
* `--replay <ndjson>` mode (`sdk/cli/src/main.rs:92`) draws the final buffer and exits
  deterministically — useful for golden-file diffing without a live pane.

## Gotchas

* **Budget**: `tests/budget.rs` enforces an 800-LOC cap on every `src/` file and checks no
  `async` appears in `view*.rs`. New render tests go in `tests/` (no cap there).
* **`Message` size**: every `Message` variant must be ≤ 128 bytes (`tests/budget.rs`).
  Box large payloads.
* **Rmux session names must be unique.** If a previous run left a session alive,
  `start_session` kills it automatically — but check for orphans with `rmux ls` if a test
  behaves oddly.
* **Screen Recording permission** for Ghostty + `screencapture`: System Settings →
  Privacy & Security → Screen Recording → enable the terminal running the script.

```rust
    let buf = render_to_buffer(&mut model, 80, 24);
```

**Layout at a specific size** — the committed breakpoints are documented in
[`references/tier1-test-api.md`](references/tier1-test-api.md#layout-breakpoints-sdktuitestslayoutrs)
(source: `sdk/tui/tests/layout.rs`):

| Size       | What to check                                                            |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `120 × 36` | Spectrum/auto-demo target — logo + all panels visible                    |
| `80 × 24`  | Standard small terminal — no overflow, table readable                    |
| `80 × 33`  | Logo present (content area = 31 rows, the exact threshold)               |
| `80 × 32`  | Logo absent — name/hint/prompt/commands still render (content = 30 rows) |
| `10 × 5`   | Narrow — should not panic                                                |
| `1 × 33`   | Very narrow at logo threshold height — should not panic                  |

***

## 2. Tier 2 — live real binary via rmux (ad-hoc verification)

Use when Tier 1 isn't enough: mouse capture, truecolor Spectrum theme, a real TTY
interaction the in-process harness can't simulate.

**Generic runner — simplest path:**

```bash

  --dataset packages/design-data \
  --steps path/to/steps.txt
```

Step file format (one directive per line):

```
# Comments are ignored

type query property=accent-color
send Enter
wait accent-color
expect accent-color
refute Error
```

Directives: `send KEY` (rmux key name), `type TEXT` (typed with 60 ms animation delay),
`literal TEXT` (send text with no key interpretation, no animation), `wait REGEX` (block
until pattern appears, 120 s timeout), `quiet [N]` (wait until pane stable for N polls),
`expect REGEX` (assert present), `refute REGEX` (assert absent), `capture` (print current
screen to stdout), `sleep N` (sleep N seconds).

The runner prints the pane contents after each `capture` or `expect`/`refute` — read those
to visually confirm layout. Exit code is 0 only when all assertions pass.

**Escape hatch — source `rmux-drive.sh` directly for a custom one-off:**

```bash
source tools/demo/auto/lib/rmux-drive.sh

start_session dd-verify "design-data packages/design-data --theme spectrum --no-resume-wizard"
wait_for dd-verify "commands" 30          # wait for home screen
send_literal dd-verify ":"
type_keys dd-verify "query property=accent-color"
send_keys dd-verify "Enter"
wait_for dd-verify "accent-color"
assert_contains dd-verify "accent-color" "token row present"
capture dd-verify                         # print for agent to read
print_summary verify
end_session dd-verify
```

helper reference (source: `tools/demo/auto/lib/rmux-drive.sh`).

